data.title: SpaceX Stock Falls Below $135 after Second Unlock — What Comes Next?
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) stock fell 2% at Friday's market open, after dropping 4.1% on Thursday. The stock slipped below its $135 IPO price as about 319 million shares became eligible for trading. Trading volume also jumped above normal levels, suggesting the latest unlock added pressure to the stock.

SPCX Share Unlock: Why the Stock Fell

Yesterday's unlock came just weeks after an even larger 912 million-share unlock on August 6, 2026. Together, more than 1.2 billion shares have now entered the tradable float in a short period. That has sharply increased the supply of shares available to investors and roughly doubled the tradable float.

SpaceX has a set lockup plan for shares held by staff, early backers and other pre-IPO holders. So, the shares are coming to market in waves, not all at once. More early holders can now sell their shares. The added supply has also led to higher-than-usual trading volume, even as SpaceX has kept up strong growth.

Other Factors Impacting SPCX Stock

SpaceX is reportedly interested in Grain Management's $6 billion spectrum portfolio, which could support its satellite-to-phone service. AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) is also said to be eyeing the same licenses. The licenses became available after Grain completed a spectrum swap with T-Mobile (TMUS) earlier this month.

Meanwhile, Anthropic is reportedly targeting an IPO by the end of 2026 that could match or top SpaceX's record $86 billion IPO valuation. Bloomberg reports that Anthropic could file for an IPO as soon as the end of August. The comparison keeps SPCX stock in focus.

What Comes Next?

The next big tests for SPCX stock will come as more shares become available. Two more releases are expected in October, with each freeing about 328 million shares. An even bigger test could come after SpaceX reports its Q3 results in November. That would put much more new supply on the market than the recent August unlocks.

More shares could then unlock as the main post-IPO lock-up period ends in December. Meanwhile, Elon Musk's 6.42 billion shares remain locked until June 2027.

For investors, SPCX stock could see more price swings around each unlock date as more shares become available. The company will need continued business growth to offset the added share supply. Strong earnings, Starlink growth, and progress on Starship could help investors absorb the new shares.

SPCX stock has a Moderate Buy consensus rating on TipRanks based on 24 Buys, five Holds, and three Sells assigned after its IPO. The average price target for SpaceX is $232.35, implying an upside of 76% from the current price.

data.title: SanDisk (SNDK) Stock Slips Despite New NAS SSDs for Prosumers and Small Businesses
data.description:
SanDisk (SNDK) stock slipped 0.65% on Friday, even after the data storage company announced two new SSDs built for network-attached storage systems. The SanDisk NAS 600 SATA SSD and SanDisk NAS 800 NVMe SSD are aimed at prosumers and small businesses that need fast storage for large files and shared work. Both drives are built for high use and can run in NAS systems around the clock.

Summer Sale - Claim 70% Off TipRanks

Two ETFs for long or short leverage on SNDK

The SanDisk NAS 600 SATA SSD is aimed at users moving from hard drives to SSD storage. It offers up to 2,500 TBW and up to 4TB of storage. SanDisk noted that the drive can reach read speeds of up to 560MB per second. It is made for multi-user work and can also serve as a cache or storage tier in a NAS setup.

The SanDisk NAS 800 NVMe SSD is built for more demanding use. It uses PCIe 5.0 and offers up to 14 PBW of endurance on the 7.68TB model. SanDisk said it can reach up to 14,900MB per second in sequential reads. The drive is aimed at tasks such as databases, virtual machines, content work and local AI.

"The way users employ NAS has fundamentally changed," said Anil Moolchandani, Vice President of Product Management at SanDisk. He said users are managing larger data sets and need storage that can run all day. Both drives will go on sale in September. The NAS 600 will start at $179.99, while the NAS 800 will start at $309.99.

SanDisk Targets Smaller Customers Amid the AI Boom

SanDisk's decision to focus on smaller customers during the AI boom makes sense. AI is constantly changing, with new developments making it easier for non-professional users to take advantage of. With that comes an increased demand for the ability to host AI agents at home or in small businesses.

However, one key problem with this has been the demand for data storage devices. AI data centers have scooped up SSDs and HDDs for their AI servers. This has left smaller customers paying much more for data storage options. If SanDisk can reach these customers, it could extend its reach to even more clients.

Is SanDisk Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for SanDisk is Strong Buy, based on 14 Buy and two Hold ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average SNDK stock price target of $2,203.13, representing a potential 38.55% upside for the shares. (See SNDK Stock Forecast)

data.title: Why Is Penny Stock Werewolf Therapeutics (HOWL) Up Today?
data.description:
Werewolf Therapeutics (HOWL) stock rocketed higher on Friday after the biopharmaceutical company announced a merger with Ambros Therapeutics. The companies have agreed to merge in an all-stock deal focused on developing neridronate for Complex Regional Pain Syndrome Type 1. After the deal closes, the combined company will be called Ambros Therapeutics and is expected to trade under the AMBX ticker on Nasdaq. The deal is expected to close by the first quarter of 2027.

Investors will note that the two companies also secured $150 million in new funding from a group of healthcare investors. The private placement is set to close at the same time as the merger. Ambros Therapeutics expects the cash to fund its work through Phase 3 results in 2028 and a planned FDA filing. The company expects to have cash to continue operations into the first half of 2029.

Neridronate is being tested in the CRPS-RISE Phase 3 trial. The study will test the drug in patients with warm CRPS-1 and track changes in pain over 12 weeks. CRPS-1 is a chronic pain condition that causes ongoing pain in an arm or leg after an injury. Ambros Therapeutics said the FDA has agreed that positive results from one key Phase 3 trial could support a U.S. approval.

"We are uniquely positioned to be advancing neridronate," said Jay Hagan, CEO of Ambros Therapeutics. He said the new funding should let the company reach its Phase 3 results and prepare for a possible FDA filing. Under the terms of the deal, former Ambros Therapeutics stockholders are expected to own about 71.7% of the combined company, while current Werewolf Therapeutics stockholders are expected to own about 6.8%.

Werewolf Therapeutics Stock Movement Today

Investors were excited about today's merger news, which sent shares of HOWL stock 127.23% higher in premarket trading. This builds on a 5.35% rally yesterday. However, the stock was still down 31.88% year-to-date and 67.33% over the past 12 months.

With today's news came heavy trading of HOWL stock, as some 94 million shares changed hands. For comparison, the company's three-month average daily trading volume was about 1.22 million shares.

Turning to Wall Street, Werewolf Therapeutics lacks traditional analyst coverage. Fortunately, TipRanks' AI analyst Spark has it covered. data.title: Broadcom Earnings Outlook – Mizuho 5-Star Analyst Flags 4 Key Questions Ahead of Earnings
data.description:
Custom chip supplier Broadcom (AVGO) is heading into its Q3 FY26 earnings report with investors focused on the strength of its AI business and the sustainability of its growth. Mizuho Securities analyst Vijay Rakesh reiterated his Buy rating and $530 price target, implying 45.6% upside potential.

Rakesh believes Broadcom has the technology needed to support Google's (GOOGL) large-scale TPU deployments across multiple chip generations, thanks to its strength in custom ASICs, SerDes, and advanced packaging. However, he noted that Google could seek lower-cost suppliers and diversify its TPU partnerships, creating a potential risk for Broadcom.

Ahead of the results, here are four key questions the analyst expects investors to focus on.

1. Can AI Revenue Beat Expectations?

Broadcom currently expects more than $100 billion in AI revenue in fiscal 2027. Wall Street expects about $121 billion, while Rakesh is forecasting $141 billion. Investors will want to know whether Broadcom can maintain its strong momentum as demand for custom AI chips grows.

Investors will want to know whether Broadcom can maintain its strong momentum as demand for custom AI chips grows.

2. How Strong Will AI Growth Be Through 2028?

Rakesh expects Broadcom's AI business to benefit from several large deployments involving Google, Anthropic, Meta (META), OpenAI, and Apollo/Blackstone (BX). Investors are looking for more clarity on the planned 20GW AI build-out, including 5GW in 2027 and 15GW in 2028.

These projects could create a significant pipeline of custom AI chip demand, potentially providing upside to Broadcom's 2028 and 2029 results.

3. How Much Can Google's TPU Business Grow?

Google remains particularly important to Broadcom because of its role in the company's AI chip business. However, investors are concerned that Google could diversify its supplier base and work with companies such as MediaTek, Alchip, GUC, AMD (AMD), and Marvell (MRVL).

MediaTek could take some of Broadcom's share of Google's TPU business in 2028 as it ramps up its own TPU chips. Rakesh will be watching whether Broadcom can maintain its position as Google expands TPU deployments and competing programs ramp up through 2027 and 2028. Any signs that Broadcom is retaining or increasing its share of Google's TPU business could strengthen the AI growth outlook.

4. What About Packaging, Margins and Buybacks?

First, Rakesh wants to see whether Broadcom's advanced packaging technologies, including CoPoS and EMIBT, can support the ramp-up of AI ASICs through 2028-29. He also expects investors to focus on long-term profit margins, particularly as Broadcom faces more competition in AI ASICs and its business mix shifts between semiconductors and software.

Finally, Rakesh sees potential for large share buybacks, as he expects Broadcom to generate more than $100 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2027 and beyond.

Rakesh is a five-star analyst on TipRanks, ranking #5 out of the 12,488 analysts tracked. He has a 69% success rate and an average return per rating of 72.40%.

data.title: Nvidia Stock Sits 8% Off Highs: Should You Buy NVDA Before August 26 Earnings?
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) stock is about 8% below its record high as investors gear up for its fiscal Q2 earnings on August 26. NVDA is trading near $216, down from its all-time high of $235.40. Analysts expect EPS of $2.09, nearly double the $1.05 reported a year ago, while revenue is forecast to jump 95% year-over-year. With growth still strong, the main risk is not a weak report but high expectations. Investors may want more than a solid beat and strong guidance to push the stock higher.

According to the TipRanks Options tool, traders are pricing in a 6% move in either direction after the results. Over the past four quarters, the stock has averaged a 2.7% one-day move in absolute terms after earnings. That's well below the current implied move of 6%. This suggests traders are paying more than usual for protection or to bet on a big earnings-driven move.

Why a Strong Nvidia Report May Not Lift NVDA Stock

Nvidia guided for $91.0 billion in fiscal Q2 revenue. Meanwhile, analysts expect about $92 billion in revenue. There are signs Nvidia could beat its own Q2 revenue forecast. Other big cloud firms and companies that make data-center gear are still spending heavily on AI infrastructure. At the same time, demand for AI chips remains higher than supply.

The main risk is that NVDA stock stays flat even if Nvidia reports strong results. That happened after its Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings in May. Despite solid results, the stock fell about 1.8% to 2% on May 21, the day after the May 20 report. This is mainly because good results were already priced into NVDA stock. So even though the company delivered solid numbers, the report may not have been strong enough to beat the market's high expectations.

Still, Nvidia's strong cash flow could help limit downside risk. The company reported $49 billion in free cash flow for fiscal Q1 2027. The company's ability to generate strong cash flow while returning money to shareholders could also keep the stock attractive to large investors.

Institutional buying may provide another layer of support, as large investors may see pullbacks as opportunities to add to their positions.

Is NVDA a Good Stock to Buy Now?

On Wall Street, Nvidia's shares continue to boast a Strong Buy consensus rating from analysts. This is based on 32 Buys and one Hold assigned over the past three months. The average NVDA price target of $305.86 suggests about 41% upside. (see NVDA stock forecast).
